title: PDF Solutions’ Exensio Was Built for Semiconductor Analytics. The New Exensio Aurora Architecture Is Built for Semiconductor Intelligence. - Semiwiki
gist: PDF Solutions is re-architecting its Exensio manufacturing-analytics platform as Exensio Aurora, a petabyte-scale architecture for secure agentic AI across fabs and supply chain, positioned as industrial-strength AI versus a general cloud LLM, with a stated ~25x performance gain and a longer-term 'agentic virtual senior engineer' goal.

insights.claim: The semiconductor industry does not have a shortage of data but a shortage of ways to turn that data into useful manufacturing insights quickly enough to matter.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Frames the analytics bottleneck that Exensio and Aurora target.

insights.claim: Advanced packaging, globally distributed manufacturing and growing product complexity are generating enormous multidimensional data that conventional analytics force engineers to down-scope.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Rising data scale is outgrowing legacy fab analytics tools.

insights.claim: Dumping all data into a general-purpose cloud LLM is useful for experimentation but not for mission-critical semiconductor manufacturing, which needs industrial-strength AI with controlled IP, reliability, repeatability, deployment flexibility and cost control.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Positions Aurora against generic cloud LLMs on trust and control, a key enterprise differentiator.

insights.claim: Exensio Aurora is a new highly scalable architecture purpose-built to handle semiconductor manufacturing data at petabyte scale and to securely deploy agentic AI across manufacturing operations and the supply chain.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Defines the product as an AI-native re-platforming of Exensio.

insights.claim: PDF Solutions cites roughly 25x faster performance at comparable hardware cost for large data sets versus conventional tools.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Headline efficiency claim to validate against real workloads.

insights.claim: Exensio Aurora's Manufacturing Data House and workflows encode analytics, rules, ML pipelines and best-practice playbooks that act as guardrails to improve repeatability and reduce AI hallucination.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Embedding engineering knowledge as executable guardrails is the reliability differentiator.

insights.claim: PDF Solutions' longer-term goal is an agentic virtual senior engineer that reduces manufacturing issue-resolution time by determining and running whatever analyses are needed.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Points to the aspirational endgame of autonomous fab troubleshooting.

insights.claim: Aurora connects model development with the Manufacturing Data House so model outputs write back into the environment, following a Data to Model Creation to Model Inference to Insights to Actions loop.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Closed-loop data-to-action makes AI part of the manufacturing system rather than a bolt-on.

insights.claim: The first public demonstrations of Exensio Aurora will take place at PDF Solutions CONNECT 2026 on October 15-16 in San Francisco.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Concrete near-term catalyst and validation event for the product claims.
